label: THE UPSTAIRS COPY
openingMemo: For the registered guests upstairs: pull up the chair with a clear view of the board. I like a sportsbook before the first rush, when you can hear the ticket printer and nobody has appointed himself the smartest man in the room. Give me a coffee, a clean rotation sheet and a little space for the blue pen. We have sixteen games to get through.

Graham Mercer has made the numbers. I have his Private Line beside the dated Pinnacle board, and this is my read of the difference. I am interested in what we would be asked to lay, what we would be getting with the dog, and which personnel questions are already paid for in Graham’s arithmetic. You can like a football team all the way from the valet stand to the window. The ticket still has to carry the right number.

Philadelphia gets the first paper clip: Graham eight, Pinnacle four and a half. The Giants and Denver are next. Green Bay needs the blue pen on both team names because the two sheets disagree about who should be favored. Those are the conversations worth having at this table. A fellow announcing that he loves six favorites can have the next booth.

The first whistle is Wednesday, then we have the Melbourne game Thursday. Sunday brings eight games at ten and four more at 1:25, our time. Have your reading done before breakfast. By the time the room is standing three deep, the cocktail server is carrying a full tray and every television has become somebody’s personal grievance, I want the questions written down already. There is no order attached to this fax. There is plenty here worth our time.
scheduleMemo: Here is the whole rotation in kickoff order, all times Pacific—the clock on the wall here in Vegas. Wednesday and Thursday get their own attention. Sunday’s eight-game 10:00 rush and four-game 13:25 wave need their homework finished upstairs; the line at the window is a poor place to start handicapping. Sunday night and Monday keep their own pages open.
changeMemo: A FRESH COPY FOR THE SUITE: I have gone back through the wording of the opening fax. The football opinion and every number are the same September 8 board. This is an editorial revision, with no fresh market pull or new personnel report tucked into it. Keep the earlier copy if you like to see what changed; the original is in the archive.

DATES ON THE PAPER: Graham’s completed September 8 information review is the basis here. His individual fair numbers keep their original dates and provisional status, and each Pinnacle quote carries its observation time. Fresh paper does not make an old quote available at the window.

THE BOARD HAS HELD: All sixteen saved MKT deltas are zero between the retained baseline and the printed observation. That tells us the quoted spreads stood still over that interval. The distance between Graham’s number and Pinnacle’s is a separate matter. Nobody gets to turn a quiet screen into a story about a steam move.

WHEN YOU WILL HEAR FROM ME: A proper opening fax, then another if the week gives us something worth putting under your door—a changed number, material personnel news or a meaningful market change. This sheet is updated by request. I can sit through a quiet afternoon without sending the hotel another page.

reviews.read: Seattle three and a half on Graham’s paper, three on the Pinnacle copy. The hook—that extra half-point above three—is the whole discussion here. I have it circled, but I am not making the opener the best game of the week just because it is the first one on the big screen. Half a point is a modest disagreement; the final personnel picture gets checked before we give it more weight. Wednesday runs out of clock first. That buys this page my attention before the Sunday stack.
reviews.note: Opening night will have enough action without us inventing some. Personnel first.

reviews.read: The Rams are laying two in Graham’s book and three and a half on the benchmark. That is a point and a half toward the San Francisco side of the counter. Before anyone starts talking home-field advantage over coffee: this one is in Melbourne, and Graham has already made it neutral. The receiver adjustment is in there too. I do not pay the same room charge twice, and I am not deducting the same football adjustment twice. This is the Thursday page to finish once Seattle is put to bed.
reviews.note: “Home team” on the rotation sheet does not move Los Angeles to Australia.

reviews.read: Chicago is the chalk on both sheets. Graham would make the Bears lay one; Pinnacle’s printed number is two and a half. That puts the point-and-a-half disagreement with Carolina. I am perfectly comfortable listening to someone tell me Chicago is the better club. Then I want to know what he is laying. A dog does not need to win the argument about which team looks prettier getting off the bus. Keep the Panthers in the morning review pile and keep the team opinion separate from the asking price.
reviews.note: Ask him what number he likes. Everybody in the lounge likes a team.

reviews.read: Baltimore three and a half, both columns. I can set this page down without feeling I have missed the afternoon. Graham’s latest personnel review did not change the displayed fair, and there is no spread disagreement here to go chasing through the race book. We come back if the information or the benchmark changes. Until then, give the time to the pages where the numbers actually separate. A full rotation sheet does not mean every game owes us a conversation.
reviews.note: Ravens three and a half on both. Finish the coffee; turn the page.

reviews.read: Here is the sort of half-point a ticket writer will hear about all afternoon: Pittsburgh three from Graham, three and a half on the Pinnacle copy. Atlanta has the favorable side of that difference, with the hook sitting above three. It deserves a circle because of where it sits, not a speech because I have a blue pen. The offered spread and the price attached to it still need checking together. Put a neat mark beside the Falcons and leave room for the larger morning questions.
reviews.note: A hook is half a point. It does not become a whole handicap because you underline it.

reviews.read: Cleveland is getting nine and a half on the benchmark against Graham’s Jacksonville seven. Two and a half points toward the Browns gets me to put the cup down. Now read the small print: Graham has already allowed for Cleveland’s quarterback re-entry uncertainty. That question needs another look, not another automatic deduction. Getting a bigger start with the dog is only interesting if the number underneath it can stand up. This is one of the first pages I want back on the table before the Sunday morning rush.
reviews.note: The quarterback allowance is already on the bill. Check it; do not pay it twice.

reviews.read: Cincinnati three from Graham, four on the benchmark. The extra point puts Tampa Bay on my side of the conversation. I want the complete quote written beside it—spread and juice—before anyone repeats “Tampa plus four” across the lounge as if that finishes the work. On this dated comparison it is a one-point question, behind the larger morning gaps. Worth its place on the sheet, certainly. It has not earned a trip to the window.
reviews.note: “Plus four” is half the quote. Write down what it costs.

reviews.read: Tennessee is the morning favorite I want to spend some time on. Graham makes the Titans three and a half; the benchmark asks them to lay one. Same favorite, two and a half points of disagreement about the job it should be asked to do. That page stays near the top of the stack. I want the current personnel picture reconciled and that separation checked again before the next edition. A friendly-looking short favorite can sell itself around a sportsbook. I want to know whether Graham’s margin still holds up.
reviews.note: Titans: top of the breakfast pile. Check why the asking price is so much shorter.

reviews.read: Detroit five on Graham’s sheet, seven on Pinnacle’s. New Orleans is getting two more points in the comparison than Graham would allow. I do not need a Saints jersey over the chair to find that worth reading. The Detroit personnel adjustments are already included in his five; the work now is to find out whether later information changes them. Give this page its time before Sunday. Once eight games are kicking off, shouting over the televisions will not improve an unfinished number.
reviews.note: Saints on the question list. Detroit’s existing adjustments have already been counted.

reviews.read: Graham has Buffalo laying two and a half, with Buffalo one on the benchmark. Both columns have the Bills favored; the point and a half between them is what brings this page to the upstairs table. It belongs alongside Carolina, after we have worked through the larger morning disagreements. If somebody comes over with a new number, write the time beside it and ask which column changed. Graham revising his opinion and a sportsbook changing its price are two different conversations. I like to finish one before starting the other.
reviews.note: Two columns, two dates. Leave enough room on the paper to keep them straight.

reviews.read: Arizona is catching ten and a half on the Pinnacle copy. Graham makes the Chargers eight. That is two and a half points toward the dog, and it earns a good seat in the afternoon stack. Double-digit chalk asks a favorite to do a fair bit of work; I want to know why Graham is asking for less. His Chargers personnel adjustment is already in the eight. Recheck the later line and personnel picture against that number before drawing a fresh conclusion. There is enough separation here to warrant the longer conversation.
reviews.note: Chargers eight or ten and a half: write the assignment down before praising the team.

reviews.read: Read this one out loud at the table: Graham has Green Bay laying one and a half. Pinnacle has Minnesota laying one. We have changed favorites, not merely misplaced a hook. Add the two sides of pick’em and the disagreement is two and a half points toward the Packers. This is why I want the team name written beside every number. A hurried “one and a half against one” can turn a real question into bad arithmetic. Green Bay gets a proper personnel and information check before we decide why the sheets face opposite ways.
reviews.note: Packers favored on Graham’s paper. Vikings favored on Pinnacle’s. Both names circled.

reviews.read: The hometown game does not get to cut the line at my table. Graham makes the Raiders three, the benchmark three and a half; Miami has the half-point difference, with the hook above three. Record it properly. Then remember that Philadelphia, Arizona and Green Bay have bigger questions in this same window. I enjoy the room when the Raiders are on, but the zip code is not another point in the handicap. This stays a short page unless the facts give us more to say.
reviews.note: The local club gets the big screen. It still has to earn its place on the sheet.

reviews.read: Philadelphia gets the paper clip. Graham makes the Eagles eight against four and a half on the benchmark—the widest separation on this fax, three and a half points toward Philadelphia. That is where I want the quiet chair and the uninterrupted time. The Washington tackle adjustment is already built into Graham’s number. I want to go back over how well that personnel assessment holds up, because a gap this size deserves a sound explanation. No pounding the table, no sending a friend downstairs ahead of the work. This is the first afternoon file I reopen.
reviews.note: Biggest gap. Longest conversation. Keep the paper clip on it.

reviews.read: Sunday night will supply its own noise. On this copy Graham has the Giants favored by a half; Pinnacle has Dallas laying two and a half. Three points apart and different favorites. Before a Cowboys conversation takes over the booth, go back to the personnel page: the Dallas adjustment and an unresolved New York allowance are both already in Graham’s source. The extra days give us time to settle those questions. They do not settle them for us. I am keeping this page open through the weekend, with both team names plainly marked.
reviews.note: Giants on Graham’s side, Dallas on Pinnacle’s. Bring the personnel update, not the bar argument.

reviews.read: Monday is its own appointment. Graham makes Denver–Kansas City pick’em; the benchmark has the Chiefs laying three. That puts three points toward Denver in the comparison, enough to keep this page beside the Giants. Graham still carries a Kansas City quarterback-clearance allowance and a Denver edge-absence adjustment. Those questions need Monday’s proper check; Saturday’s fax cannot clear them by staying in your pocket. And whatever happened to Sunday’s tickets has no business making this number for us. We start Monday with a clean page.
reviews.note: Monday dinner can be reserved on Saturday. Monday’s final opinion cannot.

closingWatchlist: BEFORE THE FIRST KICK: Seattle’s personnel check gets finished first. After that, turn to San Francisco and the Rams. Graham’s Melbourne number already has the neutral ground and receiver adjustment in it. Put a clip on those two pages; Wednesday and Thursday will not wait for the Sunday crowd to arrive.

SUNDAY, BEFORE BREAKFAST: Tennessee and Cleveland lead the morning questions at two and a half points apiece, then New Orleans at two. Carolina and Buffalo belong beside them. I want those five pages read before the coffee shop starts calling names. Eight kickoffs at once leave you enough to watch without discovering unfinished homework in your jacket pocket.

THE AFTERNOON TABLE: Philadelphia gets the long conversation—three and a half points between Graham and the benchmark. Arizona and Green Bay have two and a half each. With the Packers, say the favorite out loud: Graham has Green Bay, Pinnacle has Minnesota. The Raiders game can draw plenty of room talk; its half-point difference still goes behind those three on my sheet.

KEEP TWO PAGES FOR LATER: The Giants and Denver each have a three-point disagreement. Their personnel questions stay open for the proper game-day check. Sunday night and Monday are separate appointments. Do not let the afternoon’s result, good or bad, volunteer either one as the evening’s recovery plan.

BEFORE YOU GO DOWNSTAIRS: No order on this copy. None of the sixteen source games has a proposed wager attached. The marks tell you where I want another look; any eventual ticket still needs the execution desk’s qualification and a price you can actually get. Keep this fax folded inside the rotation sheet. The hotel can take care of dinner. We still have to take care of the number.
signature: Leave me the corner seat and a working pen. If the number changes, write it down before you tell me the story. — Bill
currentMood: Week 1 from the upstairs sportsbook table: warm with his guests, dry about the room, exact with Graham’s numbers. Philadelphia gets the paper clip; the Giants, Denver and the Green Bay favorite reversal get the blue pen. Same September 8 board, richer Vegas voice, no order.
